descriptor: Optical fibre, cable and data-centre connectivity
lede: One of the few fully integrated optical-fibre makers outside China, turned around by AI data-centre demand: a $1.1 billion hyperscaler deal, a record Q1 and a new target of ₹20,000 Cr revenue by FY29. The stock is up more than 10x from its low and prices in much of that plan.

short_version.text: Q1 FY27 revenue +87% to ₹1,910 Cr with a 20.8% reported EBITDA margin and record PAT of ₹197 Cr; order book ₹18,618 Cr; net cash after a ₹1,500 Cr QIP; margin guidance raised to 23%.

Five years of near-zero profits before this (cumulative ₹48 Cr), ROCE of 8% in FY26, a ~$100 million US litigation under appeal (auditors' emphasis of matter), and an order book now concentrated in one hyperscaler contract. FY29 needs revenue to grow 4x.
218x trailing earnings and ~62x EV/EBITDA, against HFCL at 67x earnings; even on Q1 annualised profit it trades near 65x.

blocks.text: STL (Sterlite Technologies, a Vedanta group company) makes glass preform, optical fibre, fibre-optic cable (including high-fibre-count IBR cables) and connectivity products such as pre-terminated data-centre assemblies (Neuralis). It sells to telecom operators, hyperscalers and neoclouds, and rural broadband programmes like BharatNet and BEAD, with plants in India, the US (South Carolina), Europe and elsewhere.

items.text: Vertical integration from glass to cable lowers cost and secures supply.
Data-centre products earn higher margins than telecom; enterprise and data centre to be ~50% of FY27 revenue.
Sells on long-term contracts, avoiding the spot market.
Demerged the global services business (STL Networks) and exited other non-core businesses.
Revenue fell from ₹6,925 Cr (FY23) to ~₹4,000 Cr before recovering to ₹4,745 Cr in FY26.
Announced 'Lakshya': ₹20,000 Cr revenue and 27%+ EBITDA margin by FY29.

blocks.title: Net profit vs operating cash flow, ₹ Cr

items.lead: Cash flow was always better than profit:
items.text: ₹2,471 Cr of operating cash flow over FY22-26 against ₹48 Cr of profit, used to cut borrowings from ₹3,834 Cr (FY23) to ₹1,942 Cr.

items.lead: Interest cover was only ~1.5x in FY26;
items.text: the QIP and Q1 cash flow made the company net cash (₹483 Cr) by June 2026.

items.lead: Return on new capital is not meaningful yet:
items.text: capital employed shrank FY24-26 as debt was repaid; the turn shows only from Q1 FY27.

items.text: Promoters (Vedanta group) hold 42.3% after the QIP; no pledge.
Foreign institutions up to 19.7% from 11.3% a year ago; domestic 13.3%.
Auditors added an emphasis of matter on the US litigation against Sterlite Technologies Inc (the Prysmian case, ~$100 million); the impact is 'not determinable'.
Key audit matter on impairment of investments in and loans to subsidiaries; ₹194 Cr of goodwill tested.
A banker wrongly paid ₹25 Cr under a letter of credit in an earlier year; recovery being pursued.
No capacity or utilisation numbers disclosed.

blocks.text: Global leaders Corning, Prysmian and Fujikura are larger; STL competes with them for hyperscaler contracts. HFCL is the closest Indian peer and also signed a ~$1.1 billion hyperscaler deal.

items.text: from glass preform to connectivity, which few makers outside China have.
785+ patents; hollow-core and multi-core fibre; won a European patent dispute with Fujikura.
already supplies almost all major hyperscalers.
germanium and helium scarce and expensive; limits output.
optical fibre has had sharp boom-bust cycles (FY24 revenue fell 41%).
the order book leans on one $1.1 billion contract.

blocks.text: The turnaround is real: record orders, margins above target and a repaired balance sheet. But the price already discounts most of the FY29 plan, which needs 4x revenue in three years in a historically cyclical industry. Only full delivery of Lakshya makes today's price look cheap.
